points.description: States that backpropagation reduces the error of a (multi-layer) network by propagating the error backwards from the output/last layer to the first layer, layer by layer, and updating the weights accordingly.
points.partial_credit: Half if it only says it reduces error or updates weights, without the backward direction/layer-by-layer idea.

points.description: States that the weight updates are based on gradients (local gradient / partial derivatives of the error) computed using the chain rule.
points.partial_credit: Half if it mentions gradients or derivatives (or gradient descent) but not the chain rule or per-layer computation.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying, in any wording, that the error is passed backwards from output to input layer, adjusting weights, using gradients/derivatives via the chain rule. Give part marks for a vague but related answer, e.g. only 'it updates weights to reduce error' or only 'uses derivatives'. Give 0 for wrong or off-topic answers, such as describing only the forward pass. Extra incorrect remarks do not cost marks unless they contradict the core idea.
